chunks: 843 - Hisham ibn al-Hakam said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: “Inform me about what prostration is permissible on and what is not permissible.”
He said: “Prostration is not permissible except on the earth or on what the earth grows, except what is eaten or worn.”
So he said to him: “May I be your ransom, what is the reason for that?”

He said: “Because prostration is humility before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so it should not be upon what is eaten or worn, because the people of the world are servants of what they eat and wear. And the one prostrating, in his prostration, is in the worship of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so it is not fitting that he place his forehead in his prostration upon the object of worship of the people of the world who have been deluded by its delusion. And prostration upon the earth is superior, because it is more far-reaching in humility and submissiveness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.أَنْبَتَتِ الْأَرْضُ: what grows from the earth, excluding certain categories
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth, the primary valid surface for sajdah
key_terms.جَبْهَتَهُ: his forehead, the part placed in sajdah
key_terms.خُضُوعٌ: humble submission and lowliness before Allah
key_terms.لُبِسَ: that which is worn, which is excluded from valid sajdah surfaces
key_terms.مَا أُكِلَ: that which is eaten, which is excluded from valid sajdah surfaces

ai.seo_question: What materials are permissible for sajdah in Shia Islam, and why is prostration on earth preferred?
ai.summary: This hadith states that sajdah is permitted only on the earth or what grows from it, excluding things that are eaten or worn. It also explains the wisdom behind this ruling: sajdah is an act of humility before Allah عزّ وجلّ, and prostrating on the earth better expresses lowliness, devotion, and detachment from worldly attachments.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.843 - Hisham ibn al-Hakam said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):
"Tell me about what is permissible to prostrate on and what is not."
Imam (as) replied: "Prostration is only permissible on the earth or what grows from the earth, except for what is eaten or worn."
Hisham then asked: "May I be your ransom, what is the reason for that?"

The Imam said: "Prostration is an act of humility before Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and it should not be on what is eaten or worn because the people of the world are slaves to what they eat and wear.
The one who prostrates in worship of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, should not place his forehead on what is worshipped by the people of the world who are deceived by its allure. Prostration on the earth is superior because it is more effective in demonstrating humility and submission to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic."
